statements.quote: We propose that quantum geometry (by which me mean the actual geometry typically imposed on Hilbert spaces by quantum mechanical axioms and not a quantized spacetime geometry) becomes dynamical in quantum gravity in a way that is consistent with the principles of unitarity and that captures some fundamental aspects of gravity, such as topology change.

statements.reading: Defines what the later papers call gravitized quantum theory: the geometry of quantum state space (the Fubini–Study metric), not spacetime, becomes dynamical. It concerns a different object from #11's rigid symplectic form ω on phase space (P2′) (my comparison).

statements.quote: (which includes a useful phenomenological limit, called the metaparticle [30]) that captures intrinsic non-commutative (as well as non-associative [36]) features of string theory

papers.summary: Gravity Research Foundation essay. It proposes that the geometry of quantum state space becomes dynamical in quantum gravity: topology change in a worldline toy model gives a non-linear Wheeler–DeWitt equation. The proposed tests are triple-path interference (Sorkin's I₃) and optical-clock redshift bounds. No dark matter, dark energy, dual coordinate or polarization, so it bears directly on none of Q1–Q11. It is where the label 'gravitized quantum theory' used by the later papers comes from.

statements.quote: Here we note that modular spacetime is a notion of quantum spacetime, corresponding to a generic polarization of quantum theory [11]. Note that in the context of modular spacetime, x^{\mu} are the usual spacetime coordinates, while p_{\nu} are dual coordinates conjugate to x .
statements.reading: In modular spacetime the 'dual coordinates conjugate to x' are the momenta p, with the canonical [x̂, p̂] = i (ℏ = 1). That is the single phase space of #11 (P1, P2′). 'Polarization' here means the modular (Zak) representation, called generic; it is not a choice between x and p.

statements.quote: In the limit of large expansion a\to\infty , the dual dimension shrinks to zero and one recovers the usual spacetime.
statements.reading: The preceding sentence rescales x → ax, p → a⁻¹p, which keeps the commutator. This is the kinematics of #11 §10's a·ã = 1 (App. A item 6), used here as a limit that recovers classical spacetime, not as an evolution in time. The record's C5 finding for this paper reads it the same way.

statements.quote: As already stated, in the context of metastring theory apart from the usual spacetime coordinates x^{\mu} one also encounters \tilde{x}_{\nu} , dual coordinates conjugate to x . These coordinates are the eigenvalues of operators which do not commute (in addition to the usual canonical commutators between coordinates and dual momenta),
statements.reading: The same words, 'dual coordinates conjugate to x', now name x̃ in the metastring. x̃ fails to commute with x 'in addition to' the canonical commutators with the 'dual momenta', so here x̃ is a further coordinate beside p, not p itself.

statements.quote: [\hat{x}^{\mu},\hat{\tilde{x}}_{\nu}]=i\pi\lambda^{2}\delta^{\mu}_{\nu}\hat{I}. This commutation relation can be deduced through a careful analysis of the zero mode sector of string theory where \lambda^{2}=\hbar\alpha^{\prime} [18], but in general, the scale \lambda depends on the context.
statements.reading: The scale is λ² = ħα′ from the string zero modes, but λ 'depends on the context'. The factor π is this paper's normalization; the other papers give iλ², 2πiλ² and 2πiℓ_s².

statements.quote: This is the decoupling limit where a modular field \phi(x,\tilde{x}) is restricted to the usual notion of a spacetime field \phi(x) (for example, a SM field), as considered in the context of EFT. In this limit metaparticles (correlated objects of visible particles and their duals, which, in turn, represent natural candidates for dark matter [10]) are reduced to canonical particles.
statements.reading: The paper's only statement of the identification: a parenthesis, proposed ('natural candidates'), citing [10]. [10] is BHM arXiv:2212.06086, plus arXiv:2111.14205, LHEP 2021 and two 2019 papers. Grammatically the antecedent of 'which' may be either the duals or the metaparticles (my reading). The 'decoupling limit' is a limit of the dual cell's size (b → ∞), not an energy scale; in it the dual sector drops out of the effective field theory.

statements.quote: Also, in the limit of large expansion b\to\infty , the dual spacetime dimension shrinks to zero and one recovers the usual spacetime notions.
statements.reading: The same rescaling, now applied to (x, x̃) through x → bx, x̃ → b⁻¹x̃. It is the limit in which the dark (dual) sector disappears from the effective theory.

statements.quote: Finally we note that, apart from metaparticles, the most spectacular empirical prediction of our approach to quantum gravity as “gravitization of the quantum” [16] is represented by the phenomena of intrinsic triple and higher order interference [29].
statements.reading: Metaparticles are counted as an empirical prediction, but the paper names no detection channel for dark matter.

papers.summary: A talk on the phase-space computation of the vacuum energy (unit cells with λε = 2π, N ~ l²/l_P², λ ~ √(l l_P)), extended to see-saw estimates of the Higgs and fermion masses. statements.quote: Metaparticles appear as natural dark matter quanta and the geometry of dual spacetime as the natural origin of dark energy.
statements.where: §3.1 'Quantum Spacetime and Quantum Relativity', item C
statements.reading: Stated as part of the authors' programme: metaparticles (the metastring's zero modes) are dark-matter quanta, and the geometry of dual spacetime is dark energy. Here the whole metaparticle, not the dual partner alone, is called dark matter.

statements.quote: This description (intrinsically non-commutative, since [x,\tilde{x}]=i , where x\equiv q/\lambda and \tilde{x}\equiv p/\epsilon and \lambda\epsilon=\hbar )
statements.reading: In the modular description of ordinary quantum mechanics, x̃ is the canonical momentum divided by an energy scale (x̃ ≡ p/ε), conjugate to x ≡ q/λ at ħ = λε. This is one phase space (q, p), as in #11 P1–P2′. Executed check: a rank-2 change of variables (scratch/r3-gravitized/scripts/bracket_rank.out, case A).

statements.quote: In our present case, this involves momenta p and their duals \tilde{p} , provided that these commute [p,\tilde{p}]=0 .
statements.reading: In the 'more elementary argument' the momenta get separate duals p̃ that commute with them. p̃ is a second momentum, not a rescaling of p.

statements.quote: This implies a new fundamental non-commutativity between spacetime and dual spacetime coordinates [q,\tilde{q}]\sim il_{P}^{2} .
statements.reading: A heuristic (Schwarzschild radius proportional to energy, combined with the uncertainty relation) gives a dual coordinate whose scale is the Planck length, not the string length.

statements.quote: Here it is natural to talk of dual spacetime \tilde{x} , [x,\tilde{x}]=i\lambda^{2} , and dual momentum space \tilde{p} , [p,\tilde{p}]=0 . (Also, [x,p]=i\hbar=[\tilde{x},\tilde{p}] .)
statements.where: §3.3 'Modular Spacetime, Born Geometry and Quantum Physics' (metaparticle)
statements.reading: For the metaparticle, x̃ is an independent coordinate with its own conjugate p̃. Executed check on the paper's Poisson brackets (eq. 3.15): the bracket matrix has rank 4 per dimension, so x̃ is not a function of (x, p), and the phase space is doubled. Every dark-matter statement in the paper sits in this setting; #11 instead polarizes one phase space.

statements.quote: Different observers see different spacetimes (slices of modular spacetime). However, different spacetimes are in linear superposition, and so fundamental length/time is consistent with the Lorentz symmetry.
statements.reading: Other spacetimes (slices) are allowed and superposed, through relative (observer-dependent) locality. They are not alternative vacua.

statements.quote: Classical spacetime label x of canonical QFT corresponds to a choice of (classical spacetime) polarization in modular (quantum) spacetime with a contextuality parameter \lambda .
statements.reading: Classical spacetime is one polarization of modular spacetime, and λ is called a 'contextuality parameter'. The record quotes this sentence (notes/literature-check.md §3).

statements.quote: (We will argue that dual particles, correlated to visible particles, represent dark matter.) If we turn on backgrounds p\to p+\phi and \tilde{p}\to\tilde{p}+\tilde{\phi} . Thus we have “dark matter” fields, \tilde{\phi}(x) , in the effective classical spacetime x description (after integrating over the dual spacetime \tilde{x} ).
statements.reading: A proposal ('we will argue'). The dark fields φ̃ are backgrounds of the dual momentum p̃, as the visible fields φ are backgrounds of p. My comparison: in #11, χ is matter in the p-polarization of the one (x, p) (P4); here dark matter attaches to a second momentum p̃ of a doubled space.

statements.quote: However, the visible \phi and invisible (dark matter) {\tilde{\phi}} do not commute. Therefore, one could say that dark matter is fuzzy from the point of view of classical spacetime.
statements.reading: The 'correlation' is stated as non-commutativity of the visible and dark fields, and 'fuzzy' follows from it. No force between the sectors is named here.

statements.quote: Classical spacetime emerges from the process of extensification (imagine one unit length in dual direction and many, N , modular cells in the spacetime direction). Spacetime emerges, in the large N limit, as a natural pointer basis in quantum theory [31].
statements.reading: An account of how the spacetime polarization emerges: extensification, with one cell in the dual direction and N in the spacetime direction, makes spacetime the pointer basis at large N (citing FLM 2016). It is neither spontaneous breaking nor a potential (compare #11 P5).

statements.quote: The dual spacetime labels can be understood as covariant “hidden variables” associated with the spacetime pointer basis, selected by quantum gravity.
statements.reading: What selects the polarization: quantum gravity selects the spacetime pointer basis, and the dual labels play the role of hidden variables.

statements.quote: The modular cells are not simply connected (there is a unit flux through each cell — this could be considered as the origin of matter/fermionic degrees of freedom; the deformations of each cell could be understood as the origin of bosonic degrees of freedom, i.e. interaction quanta).
statements.reading: Topological language for visible matter in phase space: fermions as unit flux through a cell, bosons as deformations of cells. Not linked to dark matter or to monopoles. Relevant only as background to C2's topological objects in momentum (my comparison).

statements.quote: Similarly, cosmology is an interplay between visible and dual (invisible) degrees of freedom [45].
statements.reading: Cites FKGLM 2021. The wording is close to #11 App. A item 2 ('one state, two descriptions'), but no dynamics are given (my comparison).

statements.quote: For each particle at energy E there exists a dual particle at energy \frac{\mu}{E} .
statements.reading: From the metaparticle dispersion relation E² + μ²/E² = p² + m²: a pairing of energies E ↔ μ/E, likened to antiparticles. The text does not link it to dark matter.

statements.quote: The canonical particle propagator is a highly singular \tilde{p}\to 0 (and \mu\to 0 ) limit of this expression.
statements.reading: Ordinary particles are the p̃ → 0, μ → 0 limit of metaparticles, the limit in which the dual degrees of freedom vanish.

statements.quote: Note that dual “particles” (dual fields) are natural candidates for dark matter because to leading order in \lambda
statements.reading: The identification is justified by the leading-order effective action that follows (eq. 3.8).

statements.quote: Here the A fields denote the usual Standard Model fields, and the \tilde{A} are their duals, as predicted by the general (modular) formulation of quantum theory that is sensitive to the minimal length.
statements.reading: One dual Ã for each SM field A. Eq. 3.8 reads S_eff = −∫√(g(x)g̃(x̃))[R(x) + R̃(x̃) + L_m(A(x,x̃)) + L̃_dm(Ã(x,x̃))] and writes no A–Ã cross term. To this order the two sectors share only the gravitational measure (my reading of the displayed action; whether the x–x̃ non-commutativity induces a cross term is not discussed).

statements.quote: In this leading limit, the \tilde{x} -integration in the first term defines the gravitational constant G_{N} , and in the second term produces a positive cosmological constant constant!
statements.reading: Integrating over x̃ fixes G_N (from R(x)) and gives a positive Λ (from R̃(x̃)), to leading order in λ. My comparison: #11 §10's corrected dictionary maps dual curvature to negative dark radiation instead. The two constructions differ: a doubled-space action integrated over x̃ here, a dual-frame fluid with a·ã = 1 and one lapse in #11.

statements.quote: In general, visible and dark matter degrees of freedom are correlated (via the minimal length \lambda ). This suggest the origin (from dark matter) of the observed scaling (found in galaxies, clusters, superclusters) and the universal acceleration a_{0}\sim cH/(2\pi)
statements.reading: The correlation, 'via the minimal length λ', is proposed as the origin of Milgrom-type scaling and a₀ ~ cH/(2π). This is the paper's only stated dark-matter observable, and it is astrophysical. #11, #1 and the literature-check note do not mention Milgrom, MOND or a₀ (case-sensitive grep).

statements.quote: Metaparticles can be understood as fuzzy dark matter, which in turn does point to a natural relation of vacuum energy (dark energy) and fuzzy dark matter [47, 48].
statements.reading: The form of the dark matter is fuzzy (wave-like), tied to the vacuum energy, citing Edmonds et al. 2017 (modified dark matter) and Edmonds, Erlich, Minic, Takeuchi 2024.

statements.quote: Thus every Standard Model field \phi(x) is doubled as \phi(x,\tilde{x}) and \tilde{\phi}(x,\tilde{x}) , with doubled and non-commutative arguments [x^{a},{\tilde{x}}_{b}]=i\ell_{s}^{2}\,\delta^{a}{}_{b} .
statements.where: §3.5 'Dynamical Born Geometry: Realization in String Theory'
statements.reading: A dual copy of the whole SM, one partner per field. Here the commutator scale is the string length.

statements.quote: \{\tilde{x}_{\mu},x^{\nu}\}=\pi\alpha^{\prime}\,\delta_{\mu}^{\nu},\quad\alpha^{\prime}\sim\ell_{s}^{2}.
statements.reading: A further normalization in the same paper: πα′, beside iλ² (§3.3), iℓ_s² (§3.5) and 2πiℓ_s² (§5.1). The executed rank check used the three non-zero brackets of this equation.

statements.quote: The dual momentum \tilde{p} could be understood from the point of view on conserved (electric) charges and corner symmetries in quantum gravity[56, 57, 58, 59]. The dual spacetime \tilde{x} is associated with conserved dual (magnetic) charges in the same context.
statements.reading: A one-line remark in the context of corner symmetries of gravity (Strominger; Freidel, Geiller and Pranzetti; Ciambelli and Leigh): p̃ goes with conserved electric charges, x̃ with conserved dual (magnetic) charges. No magnetically charged matter, monopole or dark-matter object is proposed. It is the closest any of these papers comes to #11 §11.4's pairing of the dual polarization with magnetic charge, and only a loose echo of it (my comparison).

statements.quote: Because of its interpretation as a particle model on Born geometry, associated with the modular representation of quantum theory, the space-time on which the metaparticle propagates is ambiguous, with different choices related by what in string theory we would call T-duality.
statements.reading: Other choices of spacetime are allowed and related by T-duality. The sentence nearly repeats the abstract of FKGLM 2018 (arXiv:1812.10821; code-checked FOUND). Compare #11 P5, 'the mirror vacuum is equally lawful': here the other choices are frames related by T-duality, not vacua.

statements.quote: Therefore, the classical spacetime of EFT is just one polarization allowed in the more fundamental description, and it is tied to the contextual nature of quantum measurement.
statements.reading: The spacetime polarization is one of several allowed, and the choice is tied to measurement context.

statements.quote: The non-commutative algebraic structure of the effective metaparticle description (fixed by Born geometry) is realized in metastring theory[13, 30, 5], merely with “softening” the indeterminacy by replacing, l_{s}\to l_{eff} , where l_{eff} is the relevant effective length-scale in (3.15).
statements.reading: The scale of [x, x̃] is not fixed at the string length: it may be an effective length l_eff.

statements.quote: How could we “observe” modular spacetime? Instead of scattering particles, we could entwine them.
statements.reading: The proposed laboratory signature of modular spacetime is exchange ('entwining', an R-matrix) rather than scattering. It tests the non-commutativity, not dark matter.

statements.quote: Given the fundamental commutator, [x,\tilde{x}]=il_{P}^{2} , between spacetime x and dual spacetime \tilde{x} , discussed in Section 3,
statements.reading: Here the commutator scale is the Planck length.

statements.quote: (3) the mass-scale of the Standard Model decoupling from dark matter, M_{SM}\sim 4.5{\times}10^{14}\,\text{GeV} .
statements.reading: A named scale at which the SM decouples from dark matter.

statements.quote: [x^{\mu},\tilde{x}_{\nu}]=2\pi i\ell_{s}^{2}\,\delta^{\mu}_{\nu} , etc., corresponding to (3.15)
statements.where: §5.1 'Quantum Gravitational Roots of the Higgs Mass'
statements.reading: Another normalization, 2πiℓ_s².

statements.quote: The non-commutativity of the dual coordinates is implied by a constant and nonzero Kalb-Ramond B_{\mu\nu} -field (the axion in 4-dimensional spacetime), while dynamical backgrounds correspond to intrinsic non-associativity[41].
statements.reading: Here the x–x̃ non-commutativity is attributed to a constant B-field, a background, rather than to the canonical structure.

statements.quote: Correspondingly, the zero modes in this metastring formulation of string theory are rigid length- \ell_{s} strings that correlate each Standard Model particle with its dual,
statements.reading: One meaning of 'correlated': each metaparticle is a rigid string pairing a particle with its dual. The sentence continues after footnote 18 (next statement).

statements.quote: the latter of which furnishing the most obvious candidate dark matter[103, 104].
statements.reading: Here the dual partner alone is the dark-matter candidate (citing LHEP 2021 and BHM 2021, Universe).

statements.quote: This M_{SM} also appears in Vafa’s analysis[112], postulated as the scale at which decaying dark matter “gives a small kick to its decay products.” The fully T-dual, chirally doubled description of stringy spacetime[5], dark and visible matter mix via a Berry phase-like correlation term[103]. The mass-scale of this correlation term defines the decoupling energy, below which the dark and visible matter interact as required, only gravitationally.
statements.reading: The key coupling statement. Dark and visible matter mix through a Berry-phase-like correlation term whose mass scale is a decoupling energy; below it the two 'interact as required, only gravitationally'. I read 'as required' as an appeal to observation; the paper does not say what requires it. Vafa's decaying-dark-matter scale is reported as Vafa's postulate, not as the authors' claim. Below ~10^14 GeV this is #11's strict-P4 situation, gravity only. Greps: not repeated in 2604.19418 or 2610.19522; not in 2307.16712 v2; the cited LHEP 2021 has the Berry-phase-like term but no decoupling energy.

statements.quote: M_{SM}\simeq 4.5{\times}10^{14}\,\text{GeV} is thus naturally identifiable with this dark-matter/visible-matter decoupling scale.
statements.reading: Table 1 defines M_SM := M_CH^{1/14} M_P^{13/14}. Executed check (msm_check.out): with M_P = 1.22×10^28 eV and M_CH fixed by the table's M_Λ = 1.1×10^-3 eV, M_SM = 4.48×10^14 GeV. With round values (10^-34 eV, 10^28 eV) it is 3.7×10^14 GeV. This checks the paper's arithmetic, not its physics.

statements.quote: In our approach the CP violating phases would come from the SM calculation and the dual SM sector as well from the intrinsic CP violation of quantum gravity in the non-perturbative metastring theory.
statements.reading: The dual SM contributes CP-violating phases to the visible mixing matrices. That is an influence of the dark sector on visible-sector parameters, not a force (my reading).

statements.quote: (and its dual Standard Model of the dark sector, coming from the other E_{8} in heterotic string theory).
statements.reading: The dual SM of the dark sector comes from the heterotic string's second E8.

statements.quote: The invisible (dark) sector is spanned by the dual fields \tilde{\phi}(x,\tilde{x}) , which may well be subject to a third quantization indeterminacy because of an induced non-commutativity between visible \phi and dual (invisible/dark) \tilde{\phi} fields (fuzzy dark matter).
statements.reading: The dark fields are 'fuzzy', subject to an extra indeterminacy, because of their non-commutativity with the visible fields.

statements.quote: the ensuing indeterminacy in the parameters of the dual Standard Model (the dark sector) should then be reciprocal to the relatively high precision (small indeterminacy) of the SM parameters.
statements.reading: A qualitative prediction about the dark sector's parameters: their indeterminacy is reciprocal to the SM's precision. Not quantified.

statements.quote: We stress that metaparticles[42] (zero modes of the metastring) represent a generic prediction of metastring theory and the dark matter sector can be seen as coming from a dual Standard Model with a dynamics that is entangled/correlated with the visible Standard Model[49]. The dark matter degrees of freedom are thus tied to the dual particles to the visible SM particles[9].
statements.reading: Restates LHEP 2021's 'entangled/correlated' dynamics, which is not defined further here. The record quotes the same sentence from BHM 2023 (Symmetry), whose text this section shares.

statements.quote: Furthermore, this approach shows dark energy (modeled as the cosmological constant) to be the curvature of the dual spacetime, and naturally small[9].
statements.reading: Dark energy is a cosmological constant from dual-spacetime curvature. No w and no time dependence in this paper.

statements.quote: We note that spacetime physics is classical and background-independent, with fixed spacetime polarization and dynamical geometry of spacetime, whereas quantum physics is intrinsically probabilistic, with a dynamical polarization and fixed geometry of the space of states, and the fixed rule for computing probabilities—the Born rule.
statements.reading: In GR the spacetime polarization is fixed and the geometry dynamical; in quantum mechanics it is the reverse.

statements.quote: In turn, quantum physics (physics of matter) is intrinsically probabilistic and has a dynamical polarization \psi\to U\psi ( U^{\dagger}=U^{-1} , which preserves |\psi|^{2} ), but the geometry of quantum theory is rigidly fixed:
statements.reading: What 'dynamical polarization' means here: quantum mechanics' unitary change of basis ψ → Uψ. My comparison: this is a different notion from #11's polarization, a vacuum's choice of Lagrangian subspace (P5).

statements.quote: By combining the two central featues of spacetime and quantum physics, we are led to suggest that a self-consistent quantum theory of both spacetime and matter (also known as quantum gravity) should have both a dynamical polarization and a dynamical geometry, and should be intrinsically probabilistic.
statements.reading: In quantum gravity the polarization is to be dynamical. The paper gives no spontaneous selection, potential or order parameter.

statements.quote: Dual particles and fields in this picture model (fuzzy) dark matter, and dark energy is identified with the curvatures of the dual spacetime.
statements.where: §1.1, 'Summary of the main points of the paper'
statements.reading: The identification restated as a summary claim.

statements.quote: In this description, the familiar and directly observable canonical spacetime ( x ) has a dual/conjugate partner—the dual spacetime ( \tilde{x} ), such that [x,\tilde{x}]=i\lambda^{2} , where \lambda denotes the fundamental length/time.

Yes, in four of the six texts read. The strength ranges from a parenthesis to a repeated proposal, and the latest text is the most hedged.
- 2203.17137 (2022) and 2303.15645 (2023): no mention of dark matter ('dark' occurs 0 times in either full text).

Two formulations alternate without comment: dark matter as the whole metaparticle (2407.06207 §3.1, §3.4; 2604.19418 §7), or as the dual partner alone (2407.06207 §3.3, §5.1; 2604.19418 §5.1, §7). answers.question: Q4
answers.answer:
The coupling comes in three layers, stated differently across the papers.
(i) Kinematic correlation. The visible φ and dark φ̃ do not commute ('dark matter is fuzzy from the point of view of classical spacetime', 2407.06207 §3.3; 2604.19418 §5.1), and 'visible and dark matter degrees of freedom are correlated (via the minimal length λ)'. Metaparticles are 'correlated objects of visible particles and their duals' (Minic 2023), 'rigid length-ℓ_s strings that correlate each Standard Model particle with its dual' (2407.06207 §5.1).
(ii) Leading-order effective action. S_eff = −∫√(g g̃)[R + R̃ + L_m(A) + L̃_dm(Ã)] writes no cross term (2407.06207 eq. 3.8; 2604.19418 eq. 5.7). My reading: to this order the sectors share only the gravitational measure.
(iii) A mixing with a scale, in 2407.06207 §5.3 only. 'Dark and visible matter mix via a Berry phase-like correlation term[103]. The mass-scale of this correlation term defines the decoupling energy, below which the dark and visible matter interact as required, only gravitationally'. The scale is identified with M_SM ≈ 4.5×10^14 GeV; executed check from the paper's definition and Table 1 inputs: 4.48×10^14 GeV. The statement is absent from 2604.19418, 2610.19522 and 2307.16712 v2. Its cited source, LHEP 2021 (arXiv:2010.15610), has the Berry-phase-like [[A, Ã]] term but no decoupling energy (greps).
'Entangled/correlated' dynamics (2407.06207 §6, from LHEP 2021) is not defined further in these papers.
Limits in which the dual sector vanishes:
- b → ∞ shrinks the dual dimension, and metaparticles 'are reduced to canonical particles' (Minic 2023);
- the canonical propagator is the 'highly singular p̃ → 0 (and μ → 0) limit' (2407.06207 §3.4);
- 'In the limit in which the physics of dual spacetime is neglected, one recovers local quantum field theory' (2604.19418 §5.1).
Against #11: below ~10^14 GeV the 2024 restatement has gravity-only interaction, as under #11's strict P4. The differences left are the non-commutativity at O(λ), the dual SM's contribution to visible CP phases, and the claimed galaxy-scale correlation (Q5).

answers.question: Q9
answers.answer:
Classical spacetime is called a choice of polarization. The papers say what selects it, but never call the selection spontaneous.
The choice: 'Classical spacetime label x of canonical QFT corresponds to a choice of (classical spacetime) polarization in modular (quantum) spacetime with a contextuality parameter λ' (2407.06207 §3.3; repeated in 2604.19418 §5.1 and 2610.19522 §3.2).
Selection:
- 'Classical spacetime emerges from the process of extensification (imagine one unit length in dual direction and many, N, modular cells in the spacetime direction). Spacetime emerges, in the large N limit, as a natural pointer basis'; the dual labels are hidden variables 'associated with the spacetime pointer basis, selected by quantum gravity' (2407.06207 §3.4, citing FLM 2016);
- 'quantum gravity picks the natural basis for measurement and classical description - the spacetime basis' (2604.19418 §5.1); 'the emergent measurement basis is the spacetime basis' (§7).
Dynamical polarization:
- 'quantum gravity ... should have both a dynamical polarization and a dynamical geometry' (2604.19418 §1.1), where quantum mechanics' 'dynamical polarization' is ψ → Uψ;
- 2610.19522 §3.2 names η 'the polarization (or locality) metric' that 'encodes the distinction between spacetime-like and dual-spacetime-like aspects of phase space'; 'Curving η means gravitizing the quantum'; gravitized quantum theory 'makes both its polarization and its probability rule dynamical'.
Other choices: 'just one polarization allowed', 'different choices related by ... T-duality' (2407.06207 §3.5), 'just one of many, and in metastring theory, different observers see different spacetimes', in superposition (2610.19522 §3.2). These are lawful as observer-dependent frames (relative locality), not as a mirror vacuum.
No potential, order parameter or spontaneous breaking is given for the polarization. 'spontan' occurs only as 'spontaneous emission' and in a reference title; the one 'order parameter' is a thermal Higgs-like field in 2407.06207 §2.3.
Against #11: P5's vacuum selection and P2′'s η as order parameter are not in these papers. The closest statement is 2610.19522's η as 'polarization (or locality) metric', posted after September 2026.
